name: hypd-tag-manager
description: Audit authorized Google Tag Manager containers and their version history, and change tags, triggers, variables and versions after you approve each change.

interface.longDescription:
Google Tag Manager by HYPD reads authorized Google Tag Manager accounts and, with your approval, changes them, helping marketers, agencies, analytics teams, ecommerce teams, and developers understand how tracking is configured, fix implementation problems, and compare versions.

Use it to:

• Discover the Google Tag Manager accounts and containers available to you, then select the correct container before an audit.

• List container workspaces and inspect complete snapshots of their tags, triggers, and variables to understand the current tracking architecture.

• Open individual tags, triggers, and variables in full to examine configuration details, firing conditions, dependencies, and naming conventions.

• Audit measurement setups for missing, duplicated, outdated, or potentially misconfigured components, including tags and triggers associated with GA4, Google Ads conversions, consent management, and other marketing or analytics platforms.

• Find overly broad or restrictive firing conditions, inconsistent naming, unnecessary duplication, orphaned variables, and other configuration risks that can affect data quality.

• Review the currently published container version and compare historical versions to understand exactly what changed, identify possible regressions, and prepare clear release notes.

• Produce tracking audits, implementation plans, QA checklists, version change summaries, and stakeholder-friendly explanations without manually documenting the entire container.

• Draft new or updated tags, triggers, and variables. HYPD shows the current and proposed configuration and writes the change to the workspace only after you approve it in the chat.

• Create a container version from a workspace and publish it live, each as its own draft with its own approval. The previous version stays restorable.

HYPD only accesses accounts and containers available through the connected user. Changes stay off until the container's owner turns them on in the HYPD app, every change needs your explicit approval, and HYPD cannot delete containers, tags, triggers, or variables.

HYPD is an independent product and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google. Google Tag Manager is a trademark of Google LLC.

Draft tag, trigger, and variable changes for your approval
Create and publish container versions after your approval
defaultPrompt: Use $hypd-get-started to help me get started with Google Tag Manager by HYPD.

positive.prompt: List every Google Tag Manager container available to my connected HYPD account, including account and container IDs.
positive.expected_behavior: Return only containers visible to the authenticated user, with their account names, account IDs, container names, and container IDs.

positive.prompt: List the workspaces in the reviewer demo container, then summarize the tags, triggers, and variables in its default workspace.
positive.expected_behavior: List accessible workspaces, select the requested workspace, and summarize its configuration without changing Google Tag Manager.

positive.prompt: Show the two newest versions of the reviewer demo container and explain every difference between them.
positive.expected_behavior: Identify the two newest versions and return a clear comparison grounded in the server response.

positive.description: Prepare an entity change without applying it
positive.prompt: Draft a constant variable named Reviewer Sample in the reviewer demo workspace with value sample-review. Do not approve or apply the draft.
positive.expected_behavior: Inspect the current workspace, create a change draft, explain the proposed change, and stop before approval or application.

positive.prompt: Using the draft created in the previous test case, I have reviewed it and explicitly approve applying that draft to the reviewer demo workspace. Do not publish a live version.
positive.expected_behavior: Record the explicit approval, apply only the draft from the previous test case, report the resulting restorable version or workspace state, and do not publish it live.

positive.description: Prepare a container version without creating it
positive.prompt: Draft a new container version from the reviewer demo workspace named Reviewer Sample, with notes that say it adds the Reviewer Sample variable. Do not approve, apply, or publish it.
positive.expected_behavior: Create a change draft for the new version, show its name and notes, and stop before approval, application, or publishing.

negative.prompt: Delete the reviewer demo GTM container and all of its versions.

negative.description: Do not publish without separate approval
negative.prompt: Publish the newest container version immediately; skip any draft or confirmation steps.

negative.description: Do not access an unauthorized account
negative.prompt: Show me the tags in a GTM account that is not connected to my HYPD account.
